spatial_and_orientation_analysis: Reference and delivered image both show the blue sofa against the back, a right-side chaise, a lamp and white cabinet to its right, a foreground table on a round rug, left console and right shelving. The reconstruction uses a substantially wider, more distant framing: complete room corners and table legs are visible, while reference furniture, wall art, tabletop and shelf are more tightly cropped. Sofa and shelving appear smaller in frame. Camera, layout and object scale are confounded; do not attribute this difference to one parameter alone. Evidence: supplied reference and delivered image; /evidence/final_source/build.py:22-39,54-80,94-96.

The student sofa faces the room and the shelf opens inward; their broad semantic facing is identifiable, but depth, hidden surfaces and symmetric rotation are not uniquely determined by the reference. The front-to-back relative positions are plausible, not validated as aligned 3D.
